results.title: Sums of Kloosterman fractions and applications
results.summary: We obtain improved bounds for bilinear and trilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions, building on the works of Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec and Bettin-Chandee. Our results use the spectral theory of automorphic forms, and save $N^{1/12} A^{1/3}$ over the trivial bound when $M = N$ and $A$ is small. In the exceptional Maass spectrum, we rely on a new large sieve inequality with averaging over the levels, which may be of independent interest. Applications include an asymptotic for the second moment of the zeta function twisted by a Dirichlet polynomial of length $T^{0.532}$ (improving Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill's $T^{0.515}$ and Dong-Robles-Zeindler's $T^{0.518}$), as well as an improved level of distribution for unbalanced convolutions (improving results of Fouvry-Radziwill, Wright, and Dong-Robles-Zeindler).

results.title: On the Distribution of Prime Factors of $\lfloor αn^2 \rfloor$
results.summary: Let $α> 0$ be irrational. We show that $ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ obeys a Gaussian distribution. That is, for $n$ chosen uniformly at random from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, the random variable $(ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to the standard Gaussian as $N$ tends to infinity. Additionally, we fully describe the distribution of $ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ for a positive rational $α$.

results.title: Pairing Powers of Pythagorean Pairs II
results.summary: Let $(a,b,c)$ be a pythagorean triple, i.e., $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Then $(c,a)$ and $(c,b)$ are hypotenuse-leg pairs (hl-pairs), i.e., pairs $(c,d)$ of positive integers such that $c^2-d^2$ is a non-zero square. An hl-pair $(c,d)$ is called a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if there is a pythagorean pair $(k,l)$, which is not a multiple of the pythagorean pair $(d,\sqrt{c^2-d^2})$, such that $(c^hk,d^hl)$ is again an hl-pair. To each hl-pair $(c,d)$ and each $h\geq 1$ we assign the elliptic curve $Γ_{c^h,d^h}: y^2=x^3+(c^{2h}-d^{2h})x^2-c^{2h}d^{2h}x$ and show that its torsion group is $\Bbb Z/2\Bbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ and that $(c,d)$ is a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if and only if $Γ_{c^h,d^h}$ has positive rank over $\mathbb Q$. In this case there are infinitely many such pythagorean pairs $(k,l)$, not multiples of each other. Moreover, every hl-pair is a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $1$ and a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $3$, and we give sufficient conditions for degree $2$. The two cases $(c,a)$ and $(c,b)$, where $a=m^2-n^2$ and $b=2mn$, are worked out separately.

results.title: Real equiangular lines in dimensions 18-20 and sharp fixed-angle bounds
results.summary: In collaboration with OpenAI's GPT-6, we prove that the maximum numbers of real equiangular lines in dimensions 18, 19, and 20 are $N(18)=57$, $N(19)=72$, and $N(20)=90$, respectively. We reduce the upper bounds to paired lattice points in sections of even unimodular lattices of rank twenty-four. Root-system estimates, exact certificates, and Golay-code arguments bound the sections. In the Leech lattice, generalized Hamming weights of a binary evaluation code give sharp bounds attained by nested sections. At prescribed cosine $1/q$, we also show that $N_{1/q}(d)=d+7$ for explicit intervals of consecutive dimensions for each odd $q\ge319$, and $N_{1/q}(d)=d+23$ on such intervals for each odd $q\ge5599$. Regular graphs in repeated Seidel blocks vary the cosine while preserving nullity, and a coherence bound proves optimality. Symmetric conference matrices give a further sharp family at quadratic irrational cosines.

results.title: The Vinogradov system in finite fields and two-source extractors with arbitrarily small min-entropy rate
results.summary: Fix $k\ge2$ and $1/(k+1)<ρ\le1$. Let $q=p^n$, where the prime $p$ is fixed and sufficiently large in terms of $k,ρ$, and $n$ tends to infinity through prime values. We show that for every $A\subseteq\F_q$ with $|A|\ge q^ρ$, the Vinogradov system of degree $k$ in $2s$ variables has at most $|A|^{2s}q^{-k/2-η}$ solutions in $A$. Here the integer $s$ and the saving $η>0$ depend only on $k,ρ,p$. At $ρ=1/(k+1)$ an example rules out every saving $η>0$ in this moment estimate. For $k=2$ the author previously proved the analogous estimate over prime fields. We deduce a power saving for the double sums of $e(xy+(xy)^2+\dots+(xy)^k)$ over any two sets of size at least $q^ρ$, where $e$ is any nontrivial additive character of $\F_q$. Choosing $k$ sufficiently large gives a polynomial two-source extractor with exponentially small error at every fixed positive min-entropy rate. The proof of the moment estimate uses the theorem of Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao on Marton's conjecture and a bound for the intersection of the moment curve with an affine subspace over $\F_p$.

results.title: Full Structure Recovery of Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes
results.summary: Linearized Reed-Solomon codes (LRS) are optimal sum-rank-metric codes that generalize both Reed-Solomon and Gabidulin codes, and benefit from excellent decoding capabilities, making them potentially interesting candidates for post-quantum code-based cryptography. Previous works have investigated the underlying geometric structure of LRS codes, identifying geometric invariants that distinguish them from random codes. Other works have proposed approaches to recovering the LRS structure from an arbitrary generator matrix, together with additional data. However, both the distinguishers and the recovery techniques proposed so far are either not fully general, or have a prohibitive computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a polynomial-time procedure for the full structure recovery of LRS codes from the sole knowledge of an arbitrary generator matrix. Our results show that, like their Hamming and rank metric counterparts, LRS codes cannot be used as they are for McEliece-like encryption. Our approach combines Overbeck-type attacks with suitable matrix manipulations and shortening techniques to recover the evaluation parameters across different ranges of code dimensions.

results.title: Monoid Representation of the Determinants of the Adjacency Matrices of 1-joined Path Graphs
results.summary: Following previous work by these authors, this paper explores all labeled path graphs joined by 1 edge where the labeling contains the information on how to join that graph. The algebraic structure that this operation has on the determinant of the adjacency matrix of the graph gives a finite monoid of matrices under matrix multiplication. We completely characterize the monoid using the representation theory discussed in Khovanov et al(2024). Finally, we demonstrate how these results can be used to find general formulas for the determinants of chains of 1-joined labeled paths.

results.title: On the Orthogonal Group of Quadratic Modules
results.summary: We classify the conjugacy classes of isometries in the orthogonal group of regular quadratic modules over Artinian local rings with finite residue fields, provided that the characteristic is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry. (More generally, the same classification holds over Henselian local rings with finite residue fields, such as the ring of $p$-adic integers.) The main idea is to lift results over finite fields to local rings by using the Henselian property. By applying these results to the residue class rings $\mathbb{Z}/(p^l)$, we also obtain a classification of the conjugacy classes of isometries of discriminant forms, under the condition that the order of the discriminant form is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry.

results.title: Recursive Word Conditioning for Higher-Dimensional Partitions: Exact Enumeration and Complexity
results.summary: Let $p_d(n)$ denote the number of $d$-dimensional partitions of weight $n$. We develop an exact enumeration method operating on recursively parsed partition words (which are shown to encode $d$-dimensional partitions), beginning with an elementary interior-part decomposition of ordinary partitions. Conditioning on an interior word block separates the preceding and succeeding nested blocks. For higher-dimensional partitions, transversely re-parsing the preceding words permits the same conditioning operation to be iterated. Recursive containment and joins carry effective floors across the cuts, while a nonnegative excess permits exact truncation and pruning. The resulting procedure is a complete row-conditioning algorithm. For every fixed $d\ge3$, we prove that it computes $p_d(0),\ldots,p_d(N)$ using at most $\exp\!\bigl(O_d(N^{(d-1)/(d+1)}\log(N+2))\bigr)$ arithmetic operations. A diagonal refinement replaces the final row-conditioning stages by coupled interlacing chains of ordinary-partition words and sharpens the bound to $\exp\!\bigl(O_d(N^{(d-1)/(d+1)})\bigr)$. The algorithms count constrained completions through reusable weight-indexed coefficients rather than enumerating finished partitions. Exact computations with these algorithms reach weights 100, 50, 45, 40 and 35 in dimensions 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, respectively. On a single 2.1\,GHz core the program computes $p_3(0),\ldots,p_3(100)$ in under four hours and each of the tables in dimensions 4--7 in under 30 minutes.

results.title: On the Density of Repeated Entries in Pascal's Triangle
results.summary: Let $N(a)$ denote the number of occurrences of the integer $a>1$ in Pascal's triangle, and set ${\mathcal E}_H=\{a\geq3:N(a)>2H\}$, $A_H(x)=|{\mathcal E}_H\cap[1,x]|.$ For every fixed $K\geq2$ we prove the expansion $A_1(x)=\sum_{k=2}^{K}(k!x)^{1/k}+O_K\!\left(x^{1/(K+1)}\right).$ Consequently, the Dirichlet series ${D}_1(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_1}a^{-s}$ extends meromorphically to $\Re s>0$, with simple poles precisely at $s=1/k$, $k\geq2$, of residue $(k!)^{1/k}/k$. For every $H\geq2$, $x\ge 3$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove $A_H(x)\le A_2(x)\leq\exp\left(\frac{2\log x}{(\log\log x)^{1/4}}\right)\ll_{\varepsilon} x^{\varepsilon}.$ Hence $D_H(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_H}a^{-s}$ is holomorphic for $\Re s>0$ when $H\geq2$, and $λ({\mathcal E}_1)=1/2, λ({\mathcal E}_H)=0\quad(H\geq2).$ Here, for a set $S\subseteq {\mathbb N}$, its exponent of convergence is $λ(S)=\inf\left\{σ>0: \sum_{n\in S}n^{-σ}<\infty\right\}.$ We also determine the logarithmic-order counting law for the classical Lind--Singmaster family of coefficients of multiplicity at least six.

results.title: Toward a human-friendly proof of a polynomial bound for the Directed Grid Theorem
results.summary: The Directed Grid Theorem of Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC 2015] states that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every digraph of directed treewidth at least $f(k)$ contains a cylindrical grid of order $k$ as a butterfly minor. Their function is not elementary, and Hatzel, Kreutzer, Garlet Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] improved it to a tower of exponentials of height $22$, by a proof in three stages through paths and cycles of well-linked sets. In this paper we prove each stage with a polynomial bound, so that $f$ can be chosen to be a polynomial of degree $20\,031\,568$. As a consequence, Younger's conjecture, proved by Reed, Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas [Combinatorica, 1996], holds with a polynomial bound: for the polynomial $f$ that we construct, every digraph without $k$ pairwise disjoint cycles has a feedback vertex set of size at most $(k-1)f(k)$. In fact, beyond cycles, we obtain polynomial packing-covering bounds for every strongly connected digraph that is a butterfly minor of a cylindrical grid.

results.title: On the equivariant Heegner point main conjecture and refined conjectures of Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer type
results.summary: In 1992, Darmon formulated refined conjectures of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer type for Heegner points, and proved the ``order of vanishing'' part of his conjectures by a development of Kolyvagin's Euler system arguments. In this paper, for good ordinary primes split in the underlying imaginary quadratic field, we prove the $p$-part of the ``leading coefficient formula'' conjectured by Darmon, as well as its derived strengthening by Bertolini-Darmon. Our method, which also offers a novel perspective on earlier results, is based on the formulation and proof of new equivariant anticyclotomic main conjectures, including an equivariant extension of Perrin-Riou's Heegner point main conjecture.

results.title: Symplectic bumpless pipe dreams
results.summary: Bumpless pipe dreams are combinatorial objects in bijection with alternating sign matrices. Double Grothendieck polynomials can be expressed as weighted sums over bumpless pipe dreams, a perspective that has led to many advances in the combinatorics of Schubert calculus and connections with integrable systems. We introduce symplectic bumpless pipe dreams and present an analogous formula for symplectic Grothendieck polynomials, which represent the equivariant K-theoretic classes of Sp(2n)-orbit closures in the flag variety. To prove this result, we construct an analogue of Lascoux's inflation on these objects, providing a combinatorial realization of the symplectic transition equations that appear in work of the first author, Marberg, and Pawlowski. We also show that certain marked symplectic bumpless pipe dreams correspond to set-valued reverse plane partitions. This allows us to give a tableau formula for a class of symplectic Grothendieck polynomials and to compute principal specializations of the corresponding symplectic Schubert polynomials, answering a question of Hamaker-Marberg-Pawlowski in the fixed-point-free case.

results.title: Non-archimedean generalisations of the Kuznetsov formulas
results.summary: In this paper we develop non-archimedean analogues of the Petersson-Kuznetsov formulas. Specifically, choosing a particular test function on either the geometric or spectral side of the formula, one may express the other side in terms of integral transforms. Such transforms involve representation theoretic Bessel functions attached to irreducible unitary admissible representations of $\text{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.

results.title: Induced Independence Levels and Signed Enumeration in Powers of Cycles
results.summary: For a graph $G$ we study the distribution of the independence numbers $α(G[S])$ over its vertex-induced subgraphs, together with signed Boolean-lattice sums over fixed independence-number levels. For the $r$th power $C_n^r$ of a cycle, we establish, in the range $n\ge 2rk+r+1$, a unique representation of each subset $S$ with $α(C_n^r[S])=k$ by an independent $k$-set and its forward neighborhood. The resulting Boolean-interval partition gives exact enumeration by subset cardinality. We also prove reconstruction of partially deleted forward neighborhoods and determine the support, signs, and multiplicities of the corresponding upper Möbius transform. For cycle squares we develop a complementary greedy-chain method for signed enumeration, with a five-transition classification and explicit staircase and two-gap cancellation identities.

architecture.title: Higher-Order Generation of First-Order Theories
architecture.summary: We introduce a logic whose formulae are finite descriptions of possibly infinite first-order theories. A theory is a set of first-order sentences, generated in our setting by a higher-order recursion scheme. Such a scheme is a finite grammar whose parameters may denote trees or operations on trees. We consider two interpretations: a model must satisfy every generated sentence under the conjunctive interpretation, and at least one under the disjunctive interpretation. For schemes of order $k=0$, these theories coincide with the regular first-order theories of Mathur et al. (POPL 2025). We generalize this representation by allowing higher-order schemes, while retaining first-order quantification in every generated sentence. We study the expressive power, model checking, and satisfiability of this logic. Over finite ordered structures, we show that disjunctive theories of existential sentences generated at order at most $k$ capture $k$-EXPTIME, for every $k\geq0$. Allowing unrestricted first-order sentences captures $(k+1)$-EXPTIME at the same scheme order, where $0$-EXPTIME denotes polynomial time. We also give model-checking algorithms in the corresponding time classes for each fixed signature, variable-name set, and order bound. For satisfiability under either interpretation, we extend several decidability results for regular theories to every order. However, we show that conjunctive satisfiability of quantifier-free theories, decidable at order zero, becomes undecidable already at order one. Finally, we recover decidable conjunctive satisfiability at every order by separating higher-order generation of Boolean structure from independent regular generation of ground atoms. Together, these results show how higher-order generation of first-order syntax captures the exponential-time hierarchy while retaining decidable satisfiability in restricted fragments.

architecture.title: Higher rewriting for strong linearly distributive coherence
architecture.summary: Rewriting is a computational method to solve word problems: deciding whether two compound expressions, or words, are equivalent with respect to a set of identities. Higher rewriting generalizes rewriting to higher-dimensional words, or cells, in higher categories. Following Guiraud and Malbos, we use higher rewriting to generalize Mac Lane's coherence theorem. Our result concerns strong linearly distributive categories: categories equipped with two unital tensor products related by invertible distributors. We show that in a strong linearly distributive category every formal diagram commutes.

architecture.title: The Equational Theory of Rational String-to-String Functions
architecture.summary: We give a sound and complete equational axiomatisation of the rational string-to-string functions, which can be seen as a transducer counterpart of the classical axiomatisations of regular languages by Salomaa [JACM'66], Krob [TCS'91], Bloom and Ésik [MSCS'93], and Kozen [IC'94]. The axioms are stated over a compositional, algebraic syntax for rational functions, namely the rational fragment of the syntax for regular functions introduced by Bojańczyk, Daviaud and Krishna [LICS'18]. The axiomatisation is finitary, as it consists of finitely many uniform families of axioms, each parameterised by the types involved. It is also purely equational: it consists only of equations, with no implication rules.

architecture.title: A Complete Axiomatisation of Distribution-Based Branching Bisimilarity for Non-Deterministic and Probabilistic Choice
architecture.summary: This paper proposes a notion of branching bisimilarity for non-deterministic probabilistic processes. In order to characterise the corresponding notion of rooted branching probabilistic bisimilarity, an equational theory is proposed for a basic, recursion-free process language with non-deterministic as well as probabilistic choice. The proof of completeness of the axiomatisation builds on the completeness of strong probabilistic bisimilarity on the one hand and on the notion of a concrete process, i.e. a process that does not display (partially) inert τ-moves, on the other hand. The approach is first presented for the non-deterministic fragment of the calculus and next generalised to incorporate probabilistic choice, too.

architecture.title: Direct cognition problem: a semantic skeleton of mathematics and its growth
architecture.summary: We construct a finite semantic skeleton from three axioms of classical propositional logic without specifying a target theorem. During growth, the constructor records which proofs share an intermediate lemma. When choosing the final anchors, it also counts inferences that use a premise the lemma can supply by substitution. The primary skeleton contains ten anchors whose certificates expand to the axioms through 27 shared inference steps. It shortens all 30 previously unseen proof structures in an external catalogue of typed combinators, saving 90 of 412 steps. One anchor recurs in all five runs of the constructor. In a post hoc test, this anchor alone shortens 26 of the 30 proofs. It also shortens 331 of 475 previously unseen proofs of familiar theorems in a second corpus.

architecture.title: Algebraic Diversity of Switching Functions
architecture.summary: Algebraic Diversity generalizes averaging over many observations to averaging one observation over a group of transformations matched to its structure. This paper develops the framework on the Boolean cube $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ for the translations, the coordinate permutations, the hyperoctahedral group, and the general linear and affine groups. It determines the commutant of each action and gives closed forms for the group-averaged second-order statistic of one truth table, which collapses to the Walsh periodogram for the translations, to per-weight averages for the hyperoctahedral group, and to the weight up to complementation for the affine group. Bent functions are exactly those whose translation average is white, the Haar transform along an input order is the multiplexer tree of Shannon's expansion, and higher-order averages see only the weight below a first informative order, two for the translations and four for the affine group. A matched stabilizer stands in for repeated observations, since a vote over orbits of $s$ points divides by $s$ the number of noisy truth tables a target error requires. The same viewpoint gives the affine hull of a function as matched coordinates, an exact variance identity for XOR hashing, and matched hashes whose variance never exceeds that of a pairwise independent hash. Applications on public benchmarks include hash choice for approximate model counting, the decision of parity-structured formulas and the refutation of counting formulas modulo 3 and 4 from the spectra of clause blocks, separation of NPN classes by canonical spectra, tested on ISCAS-85 cut functions and all five-input classes, correction of noisy truth tables and protection of lookup tables by voting over symmetries, blind group matching, and an analog of the CLEAN algorithm that writes a truth table as the XOR of atoms in the fixed spaces of groups. All proofs are given in full.

architecture.title: Higher-Dimensional Automata in Geometric Logic
architecture.summary: What does the topos of a higher-dimensional automaton know about its infinite behaviour that its language does not? We write partial HDAs with an infinite run as models of a geometric theory over an intuitionistic metatheory with no choice. The topos of a machine is that of sheaves on its prefixes. The label word of a prefix records the shape and acceptance bit of each cell with the ipomset of each step. Under unique choice these words give a geometric morphism to the label topos of sheaves on label words, which thus records the shapes and acceptance bits that the Büchi language forgets. Machines sharing their Büchi language and their frames can differ over the label topos. The bouquet of two squares shares its frame and its Büchi language with the interleaved square; each accepted run of either reads the two events in parallel forever. Only the interleaved square has runs through cells of shape a, and the geometric sequent excluding such runs separates the two over the label topos. Over alphabets with decidable equality, finite rigid machines are unambiguous exactly when their label maps are inclusions of locales, and their equivalence over the label topos is decided whenever either is unambiguous. Equivalences of frames over the label topos transport points with their labels, and the invariants of fibres and of the language of points follow from this transport. On finite partial HDAs over alphabets with decidable equality, Muller and Büchi acceptance coincide exactly under a weak form of excluded middle.

architecture.title: FlashProve-Next: Verifiable Inference for Production LLM APIs
architecture.summary: Clients of closed-weight LLM APIs cannot verify whether a provider ran the advertised model, precision, hidden prompt, and reasoning budget. Existing approaches either trust hardware or third parties, or re-prove every layer of an integer surrogate at high cost while diverging from native floating-point serving. FlashProve-Next produces verifiable, zero-knowledge-masked proofs for individual LLM API responses without modifying native serving (bf16/fp8/mxfp4, random sampling, FlashAttention, CUDA graphs, batching, prefix caching) and without disclosing weights, hidden prompts, hidden reasoning, or activations (dense profiles fix coarse geometry; cross-architecture hiding is deferred). A non-depleting Reed-Solomon weight commitment model_id opens inside proofs via hidden column openings, while local per-operator rounding contracts remove integer surrogates and the refusal-bit leak. Cost-weighted spot-checking supports non-interactive public verification (NI-315, $\varepsilon \le 2^{-40}$, $Q \le 2^{64}$) and external-seed C_pre mode (ExtSeed-153, $\varepsilon \le 2^{-20}$, $Q_{\rm samp} \le 2^{30}$). Twenty-eight Lean 4 modules (696 declarations, zero sorry, standard axioms only) mechanize round-by-round soundness, bucketed sampling, $\mathbb{F}_{p^3}$ constrained-mask binding, causal masking, six IR gadgets, and executable FPN2 verifiers. Five-model Blackwell calibration gives zero false rejections across 1.85M GEMM/MoE blocks and 1.96M non-GEMM rows. Our zero-Phase-2 folded backend (folded ZK simulator open) proves Qwen3-0.6B ExtSeed-153 (1.47B cells, 8 MiB) in 450.2 s GPU (10.76 s CPU) at unique-decoding $Q=128$, passes a 14/14 cheating matrix, and scales to 36-layer Qwen3-4B (dev $4+2$) and live vLLM Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 Relation 6 (1.49 s prove, 23.4 ms Rust verify, public weight tiles). Rust fpn-verify checks 8 MiB FPN2 Relation 2 proofs in 10.1 ms on CPU.

architecture.title: Interactive Proofs as a Unified Framework for Evaluating and Leveraging Verifiable Proof Generation by LLM Agents
architecture.summary: Recent advances in LLM-assisted theorem proving and program verification have attracted widespread attention. Beyond determining whether a proposition is true, LLM agents must produce evidence that can be independently checked by humans or formal verification tools. To evaluate the underlying, protocol-agnostic ability of LLM agents to construct verifiable proofs-rather than their proficiency with any particular proof language or verification tool, we introduce Merlin-Bench. Drawing on interactive proof systems from computational complexity theory, we cast an LLM agent as the prover: under a designated protocol, the agent interacts with a formal verifier to substantiate its claimed answer to a problem instance. We develop an automated framework for constructing test cases and use it to create 100 cases across 15 problem families, each formulated within this prover-verifier framework. Experiments with 10 frontier LLMs across multiple agent harnesses show that reliably producing verifiable proofs in accordance with specified protocols remains a substantial challenge. Our case studies further provide actionable insights into improving agents' ability to generate verifier-accepted proofs: tool use is essential for completing practical proof tasks; different forms of guidance, ranging from engineering instructions to problem-specific knowledge, substantially affect success rates on interactive-proof tasks; and proof-solving experience distilled from abstract tasks can transfer to concrete, real-world verification tasks.

architecture.title: Approximate Counting and the Provability of Combinatorial Principles
architecture.summary: Understanding which axioms suffice for the provability of known results in algorithms and complexity and whether they can settle longstanding conjectures in these areas is a fundamental direction at the intersection of logic and computer science. Motivated by this research program and its applications, we investigate bounded arithmetic theories designed to serve as a logical foundation for *probabilistic reasoning*, the relation between these theories, and whether they can prove more theorems than their underlying base theory for *deterministic reasoning*. In more detail, for nearly twenty years, Jeřábek's theory $\mathsf{APC}_1$ [Jeř07a] has provided a standard framework for the formalization of results from theoretical computer science relying on probabilistic techniques. In a recent work, [CLOW26] introduced a (possibly weaker) theory called $\mathsf{APX}_1$. This theory is able to capture a large set of probabilistic arguments using four simple axioms for *approximate counting*. Both theories extend Cook's theory $\mathsf{PV}_1$ [Coo75] for deterministic polynomial-time reasoning. Our main result establishes that, in the relativized setting, $\mathsf{APX}_1$ does not prove the retraction weak pigeonhole principle ($\mathsf{rwPHP}$). Consequently, $\mathsf{APC}_1$ is not conservative over $\mathsf{APX}_1$ with respect to relativized $\forallΣ^b_1$ sentences. Moreover, we establish that the unprovability of $\mathsf{rwPHP}$ is part of a more general phenomenon: for a large class of finite combinatorial principles, the existence of an *infinite model* of the negation of the principle *characterizes* its unprovability in $\mathsf{APX}_1$. This result, which is analogous to a theorem of Riis [Rii94], implies that $\mathsf{PV}_1$ and $\mathsf{APX}_1$ prove exactly the same finite combinatorial principles of this form.

architecture.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data
architecture.summary: Procedurally generated logic problems are used to both evaluate and train reasoning in language models. Their difficulty is usually set by planting a proof, that is, by sampling a proof of the desired depth and stating its premises as the problem. However, a planted proof is only one possible proof. A problem can also have shorter proofs, or several unrelated ones, and its stated depth then overstates what solving it requires. We measure what a problem actually requires, relative to a stated set of inference rules. For each problem, we compute the steps every proof must make, the shortest proof, the number of minimal proofs and the indispensable premises, and export certificates that an independent checker verifies. Audits of eight datasets find depth that is forced (ProofWriter, Blocksworld), problems labelled depth 5 that require about two specific rule applications (FLDx2), and answers that need no particular step (ZebraLogic). We then construct problems whose every proof has a requested structure, using a catalog of shortcuts proved once per rule set. Every constructed problem is checked in full and comes with its own certificate. In training, the best data mixes depths and problem types. At equal size, such mixtures of certified problem types, including model-checking problems that forward generation does not produce, transfer better than FLDx2-style derivation data for Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 8B.

education.title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
education.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support. While offering efficiency and innovation, their deployment raises critical privacy, security, and ethical challenges due to the uniquely sensitive and longitudinal nature of telecom data. This paper presents a survey of LLM risks and safeguards in telecom context. Our survey introduces a telecom-specific taxonomy linking privacy, security, and ethics with use cases and outlines open research challenges such as longitudinal data privacy, cross-border compliance, and scalable guardrails.

education.title: Model Weights, Airlocks and Sandboxes: A Call for Technical Validation of Re-identification Tests under the EDPB Anonymisation Guidelines
education.summary: The Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB), published for consultation in July 2026, assess anonymity relative to the entities that may access data. They bring AI models into scope and call for testing, but do not say how a re-identification test should be designed or validated, or how far its result counts as evidence. Building on our reply to the consultation, we describe a framework based on a secure processing environment whose outputs are reviewed before release (an airlock), and distinguish forms of release and three types of evidence: formal, empirical and indirect. We raise seven open questions, each with a scenario, and examine their technical side in three settings: the release of model weights (the trained parameters of a machine learning model), review at an airlock, and regulatory sandboxes, in which an authority supervises development and testing. In each setting the assessment depends on how far a test result can be relied on, since a failed re-identification attempt may mean only that the test was too weak. Drawing on measurement practice in other regulated fields, we call for re-identification tests to be validated as measurement methods, with stated detection limit, bias and uncertainty.

education.title: Proverbs As A Window On Collective Prescriptions
education.summary: Proverbs, as repositories of traditional wisdom, have informed human reasoning for millennia. Yet the collective prescriptions they encode have remained largely unquantified. We introduce a computational framework to analyze nearly 50,000 English-language proverbs. Using large language models, validated against human judgments, we map the topical landscape of proverbs, assess their prescriptive power, and quantify their recommendations on key dimensions of human judgment and behavior. We find that most proverbs are prescriptive, offering guidance in domains under individual control, such as preparation and prudent action, whereas proverbs about uncontrollable circumstances, such as fate and mortality, tend to describe rather than prescribe. When prescriptive proverbs take a consistent stance, they favor caution over risk, long-term over short-term outcomes, honesty over deception, and kindness over malice, and show a moderate tendency toward suspicion over trust. On dimensions involving genuine trade-offs, especially autonomy versus compliance, proverbs provide contradicting advice rather than a single recommendation. This analysis provides a quantitative map of the collective prescriptions in a culture's proverbial wisdom, revealing a core of prudent, honest, and forward-looking guidance alongside varied advice where circumstances dictate the best course of action.

education.title: Decision and Support Mechanisms under Platform Information Overload: A Generative-Agent Experiment on College Application
education.summary: People now make major personal decisions surrounded by far more online information than they can read, yet research says little about why information overload affects some people more than others. We study this question in Chinese college applications, a high-stakes decision made amid heavy online content where each list can be scored objectively once admission cutoffs are released. We simulated 90 applicants using language-model agents with family backgrounds from a national household survey. Each applicant wrote a list of eight programs alone and revised it four times: after parent and teacher advice, after reading a feed of twenty real online items, after a mentor gave advice based on the applicant's rank, and after a second mentor offered only emotional support. After each step, we scored the list and asked how anxious the applicant felt. When applicants decided alone, admission rates were similar across socioeconomic status (SES) groups. The gap appeared once family background entered through parents and teachers: low-SES parents asked for low tuition and schools near home, leaving fewer reachable programs, so admission was 100% for high-SES vs. 77% for low-SES applicants. The platform feed gave everyone the same amount of information but did not narrow this gap; applicants maintained their decisions while reporting higher anxiety. Personalized advice cut the gap to 3 points by raising low-SES admission from 80% to 97%, but led students to higher tuition and less preferred majors. Emotional support did not further lower anxiety, but helped applicants go back and use helpful items they had ignored. These simulation results suggest that when information is abundant, more of it neither improves decisions nor reduces inequality. Personalized information does both, while moving inequality from the outcome to its cost.

education.title: Atunda: Building an Afrogenic Dance Movement Dataset for AI-Driven Classification
education.summary: This paper introduces Atunda, the first systematically collected video dataset of Afrogenic dance moves, designed for training and evaluating deep learning models for movement classification. The first phase of the dataset includes nearly 400 videos covering 13 distinct dance moves from African and African Diaspora performative culture, making it the first AI-ready resource of its kind. Using this dataset, we train and evaluate various configurations of temporal convolutional neural networks, achieving a classification accuracy exceeding 95%. The baseline results provide a benchmark for future studies in movement classification, especially in the understudied area of Afrogenic performative culture and tradition. This work lays the foundation for developing in the future digital metrics of similarity, automated attribution systems, and tools that preserve and promote the cultural heritage of Afrogenic dances.

education.title: Where Does the Asymmetry Enter? Staging a Fairness Audit Across a Fused Multimodal Moderation Pipeline
education.summary: Almost every short-video upload now passes through a classifier that fuses video, speech, and on-screen text into one decision about whether it may be seen. It moderates every language community on the platform at once, and fairness across them is judged, if at all, from one accuracy score. That score is compatible with error falling almost entirely on one language group. An audit that goes looking reads the model's decisions, the last stage of a long pipeline and the one whose test has the fewest items. We ask where in a fused pipeline a subgroup asymmetry can be detected at all: in what the classifier may read, in what its branches encode, or in what it decides. We answer this with a post-hoc audit of a published TikTok classifier, holding all three stages to one significance standard using only its logged decisions, labels, and pre-fusion features, with source language as the subgroup axis. The asymmetry is significant at the stage deciding what the model may read, and again in what the text branch encodes. At the earlier stage, a language-blind cap admits less of a Vietnamese clip than an English one, for reasons of segmentation, not verbosity. The asymmetry is undetectable at the decision, where the smallest subgroup leaves twelve items to test. An audit reading only decisions looks where its evidence is thinnest; the same test staged upstream recovers a disparity the decision-level view returns as noise.

education.title: Towards Democratized Academic LLM Hosting: Practical insights from needs, implementations, and governance across Dutch institutions
authors: the Towards Democratized Academic LLM Hosting Workshop Consortium
education.summary: Academic LLM hosting is emerging as an operational infrastructure domain with recurring socio-technical patterns, tensions, and governance requirements across institutions. Based on a workshop with academic infrastructure, research-support, education, and policy-adjacent stakeholders, this paper synthesizes current practices and open questions around institutionally governed LLM services for Dutch academia. It highlights challenges around deployment models, energy and utilization, governance, tooling, commercial integration, and research and education use cases, and identifies emerging directions for service pathways, coordination, and responsible operation.

education.title: The cost of being seen as AI in group bargaining
education.summary: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in collective decision-making, people's perceptions of AI may shape who reaches agreement and what they receive. We studied this in a repeated three-player majoritarian bargaining game with 2,234 participants. Players saw each opponent identified as Human or AI. The instructions described AI as acting either independently or on behalf of a human. Human participants made every decision. In mixed groups, players presented as AI received fewer points in opening offers, were included in fewer final agreements and earned about 18% less per round than those presented as Human. Smaller payoffs in agreements that included them accounted for most of the observed gap. Further analysis found a payoff gap even when all three players agreed. Social perceptions of AI may therefore shape who benefits from collective decisions, with potential costs for people represented by AI.

education.title: Data Centers: The Error of Generalizing Environmental and Socioeconomic Impacts. The Need for a Contextualized Assessment of Computing Infrastructure in Brazil and Worldwide
education.summary: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence and cloud computing has intensified debates about the environmental and socioeconomic impacts of data centers, including electricity and water consumption, noise, land use, and employment. A recurring methodological problem in these debates is the use of global data, or of evidence produced in a particular country, to draw conclusions about facilities located in very different settings. This paper argues that the impacts of a data center depend on the geographic, climatic, energy, technological, economic, and regulatory conditions of the territory where it operates, and must therefore be assessed at the appropriate territorial and technological scale. Using Brazil as a case, we discuss the country's predominantly renewable electricity mix and the curtailment of renewable generation, the reported prevalence of closed-loop cooling, national and municipal noise regulations, the water-efficiency requirement of the new Redata tax regime, and the ongoing litigation over the Pec{é}m data center in the state of Cear{á}. We also examine a recent study of data centers in Northern Virginia, showing the limits of its external validity and of its noise measurements. We propose a multiscale assessment framework and conclude that international evidence should inform which questions are asked, not predetermine the answers -- a principle that applies equally to claims of harm and to claims of safety.

education.title: The Socratic PAUSE: safeguarding scientific judgement at AI speed
education.summary: Generative AI can turn a tentative scientific question into hypotheses, methods, code and interpretations within minutes. Yet generating a contribution does not establish that it deserves scientific reliance: researchers must still examine its evidence, assumptions and implications, and remain accountable for the decision to rely on it. Using Einstein's sketch of scientific discovery as a lens, we argue that AI has accelerated discovery far more than justification. In human-AI research partnerships, confidence can therefore outgrow evidence through three mechanisms: recursive reinforcement, loss of provenance and miscalibrated reliance on AI-generated contributions. Verification debt accumulates when such contributions are carried into later claims or decisions without adequate scrutiny. Accordingly, we propose the Socratic Pause as a deliberate checkpoint at consequential decision gates, where an AI contribution remains provisional while a researcher examines its basis. The PAUSE protocol structures this examination through five steps: Pin down the claim, Ask and challenge, Uncover assumptions and alternatives, Scrutinise the evidence and Exercise judgement. It concludes with a recorded decision to accept, revise, reject or defer the contribution. We show how AI research tools can support this practice without displacing human judgement, and outline a framework for evaluating whether it improves verification, decision-making and independent understanding. The aim is to preserve the freedom to explore with AI while ensuring that those responsible for the work can say what was examined, what remains uncertain and why the next step is justified.

education.title: Is Sara Omar the true author of Dødevaskeren (The Dead Washer)? Authorship attribution in Danish literature
education.summary: The bestseller Dødevaskeren (The Dead Washer) was published in 2017 under the name Sara Omar. A Danish colleague has suggested that the novel may have been written by another author, possibly Mads Peder Nordbo. To investigate this authorship question, four authorship attribution methods were applied, namely Delta, intertextual distance, Nearest Shrunken Centroids (NSC), and naïve Bayes. Using various parameter settings, these approaches consistently identify Nordbo's writing style in the doubtful novel, although the results do not provide conclusive evidence that he authored the novel in its entirety. In a second step, the novel was divided into non-overlapping segments of 5,000 tokens. Once again, Nordbo's style was identified in the majority of the segments. However, a small number of passages do not clearly support this conclusion and instead suggest the possible involvement of another, as yet unidentified, author, possibly Sara Omar herself.

education.title: Silent on Code? A Computing Lens on Generative AI Guidance at Canadian Polytechnics and Research Universities
education.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools now write, explain, and debug code, which changes how computing students learn and how their work is assessed. Instructors, however, act within institutional guidance written largely with essays in mind. We report a document analysis of the public, institution-level GenAI guidance of the 13 members of Polytechnics Canada and the 15 members of the U15 Group of Canadian Research Universities, retrieved in October 2026. Using a 27-item codebook spanning governance, integrity and assessment, data and legal issues, values, AI literacy, and a computing lens, we find that both sectors leave course-level decisions to instructors, although polytechnics more often prohibit use unless the instructor permits it (8 of 13 vs. 4 of 14), and converge on disclosure, links to academic integrity policy, and, in most institutions, the expectation that programs adapt rules to their discipline. Polytechnics frame GenAI as workforce preparation substantively far more often (7 of 13 vs. 0 of 14), whereas universities more often address assessment redesign. Twelve of 27 institutions with retrievable guidance mention code, but almost always as one output type among many; none names an AI coding assistant or provides substantive code-specific guidance on attribution, assessment, or licensing. Institution-level guidance is thus not silent on code but leaves programming-specific questions largely to programs and instructors. We propose five elements of discipline-level guidance for computing and release our codebook and coded dataset.

education.title: How AI Is Reconfiguring Work in India: A Task-Based Framework for Understanding Augmentation, Displacement, New Roles and the Changing Structure of Jobs
education.summary: Public debate on AI and Indian employment tends to compress a complicated phenomenon into a single binary: will AI take a given job, or not. This paper argues that the accurate picture is a taxonomy rather than a binary. AI rarely replaces a job wholesale; more often it automates a bundle of tasks within a job, and the size of that bundle varies with task structure, sector, regulatory setting, and, distinctively in India's case, the economics of AI access itself. We propose a four-level framework (task, job, occupation, labour-market outcome) and classify Indian job impact into two broad regimes: jobs where AI has automated most of the skill bundle and the human is reduced largely to validation, and jobs where the human remains the primary driver and AI functions as a productivity tool. Each regime splits further into policy-relevant sub-types. Drawing on Indian evidence from business process outsourcing, manufacturing, MSMEs, sanitation, financial services, law, and software engineering, we show that every job in our sample has had to be reimagined, through task-level augmentation, task reallocation, or a genuinely new role built around operating the machine, rather than simply eliminated or defended unchanged. We close with a distributional analysis of who bears the cost of this reimagining and a three-pronged policy recommendation: continue encouraging AI diffusion, invest in India-specific labour-market research, and pair adoption with structured worker-transition pathways.

education.title: Language models call themselves AI but do not favor AI over people
education.summary: Many fear that AI systems will side with one another against people. Social identity theory, which explains why people favor their own group, offers one way to examine this fear. Seen through this theory, AI would side with AI only if it treated AI as its group and favored AI over people. In three experiments, 24 language models favored a group they were assigned to, even a team of AI agents. With no group assigned, they gave a person more money and credit than an AI agent. Prompts that made them say they belong with AI changed their behavior much less than an assigned team did. These models call themselves AI but do not favor AI over people. Judged by social identity theory, they show no sign of siding with AI against people.

education.title: Beyond Disclosure: Compositional Privacy Harm in AI Systems
education.summary: Privacy law attaches obligations to each stage of information processing, whether it be collection, use, storage, or disclosure. We examine how legally cognisable privacy harm emerges across this full lifecycle rather than at any single one of these points. We argue that privacy risk in AI systems is compositional, arising from the interaction of memorisation, extraction, inference and contextual transfer. Disclosure is therefore not the sole threshold of privacy harm: legally significant consequences may emerge even where no underlying record is reproduced verbatim. Drawing on contextual integrity, we argue that privacy protection must extend across the lifecycle of AI-mediated information rather than attach to disclosure alone.
